subject: Rapid patch notice — unscheduled maintenance and follow-up for degraded streaming throughput
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: [URGENT] Observed memory growth in streaming runtime — quick alignment

Team,

We just observed sustained memory growth on the streaming runtime serving some long-context workloads in the dedicated-us-west-2 pool. Symptoms: increased tail latency for streaming responses, several request retries, and a growing backlog on nodes pinned to customer Acme Analytics (dedicated shard). Initial trace (attached templog) shows a KV-cache retention anomaly when sequences exceed ~64k tokens — memory not freeing between sessions.

Immediate asks:
- David: can you validate whether the leak is in the KV cache eviction path or in the oss attention buffer? A quick bisect of the 1.2.0 -> 1.2.3 kernel changes would help.
- Rishi / Rachel: start drafting a short customer notification for any impacted customers (I’ll review). Emphasize we’re deploying a hotfix with minimal downtime and a rollback plan.
- All: prepare a 30-min maintenance window option starting ~11:30 PT if we need to restart serving nodes.

I’m beginning an internal incident doc. I can take lead on customer comms once we have an ETA.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Sr. Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Observed memory growth in streaming runtime — quick alignment

Monica — dug in and reproduced the retention locally using a stress harness that streams long contexts repeatedly. Root cause appears to be a race in the KV-cache background compaction where a pending reference prevents page freeing; it looks introduced in the 1.2.3 async refcount changes. I have a small patch that forces a safe barrier before compaction (attached patch).

I recommend a hotfix rollout: build 1.2.4-hotfix -> progressive restart of affected nodes -> monitor memory & latency. If nodes do not stabilize within 10 minutes, rollback is straightforward to 1.2.3.

I’ll be on standby to land the patch and coordinate the build.

—David
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Stokes <devon.stokes@acme-analytics.com>, Acme Platform Ops <acme-platform-ops@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Temporary performance degradation — quick notice and planned hotfix

Devon / Acme Ops team,

I wanted to notify you directly: we’ve detected degraded streaming throughput for some long-session requests affecting a subset of your dedicated capacity in us-west-2. Impact: intermittent increased tail latency and occasional retries for very long context streams (>50k tokens).

What we’re doing now: the infra team identified a memory-retention bug and is preparing a 1.2.4 hotfix. We expect a short rolling restart of affected nodes beginning at approximately 11:35 PT today; the operation should not require request-level downtime but may cause a small increase in latency for up to 10 minutes per node as it restarts. We will roll the fix progressively to avoid customer-wide disruption.

Attachments: rollout-checklist.pdf (high level steps), templog-streams-usr-1187.txt (anonymized log excerpt).

Requested from you: please confirm whether the 11:35 PT window works for your team, or if you prefer a different 30-min window today. If you have any scheduled long-running jobs, please flag them so we can coordinate.

We’ll follow up with a short post-deployment note summarizing what changed and the plan for a root-cause postmortem. Apologies for the short notice — we know this is disruptive.

Best,
Monica Patel
Sr. Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Devon Stokes <devon.stokes@acme-analytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Acme Platform Ops <acme-platform-ops@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Support <support@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary performance degradation — quick notice and planned hotfix

Thanks for the heads up, Monica. 11:35 PT is OK for us — we’ll pause any scheduled long-context runs that start between 11:15–12:30 PT. Please confirm when the patch is applied and when you’ve validated stabilization. We appreciate the transparency.

—Devon
Head of Platform, Acme Analytics
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Stokes <devon.stokes@acme-analytics.com>, Acme Platform Ops <acme-platform-ops@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Hotfix deployed — summary, validation, and next steps (post-deployment update)

Devon / Acme Ops — quick summary following the rollout:

What happened: David identified a KV-cache compaction race causing memory retention under long streaming workloads.
What we did: Deployed 1.2.4-hotfix in a progressive restart across your dedicated shard between 11:40–12:30 PT. No customer-wide outage; each node experienced a ~2–8 minute restart window.
Observed outcome: Memory usage returned to expected baselines, tail latency improved by ~65% on sampled long streams, and retries dropped to baseline. We validated using the same stress harness plus a sampling of your live streams (sanitized). Full logs attached as templog-streams-usr-1187.txt and patch attached.

Postmortem / follow-up:
- Immediate: we will keep a heightened monitor on your shard for 72 hours with 5-minute alerting windows.
- Root cause: the async refcount barrier was omitted in the compaction path in 1.2.3; fix: barrier + additional unit/test coverage for background compaction.
- Preventative: adding an e2e regression test that simulates long-context retention across multiple concurrent clients, targeted for 2026-06-25.
- Ask of Acme: if you can share any additional long-stream samples (anonymized) that hit tail latencies, that will help validate the regression test.

If anything regresses, ping me directly and we’ll escalate to an urgent rollback if needed. I’ll follow up with the postmortem doc (working draft link) and an exec summary for your ops leadership tomorrow.

Apologies again for the interruption and thanks for the fast coordination.

Best regards,
Monica Patel
Sr. Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference
